title: Guard stage_definition/settings/goal merges against missing local track before FK-constrained insert
rule: Nygard (I/O ordering race) — FK integrity on merge; matches the fix already applied to bookmark/gamification_settings/study_day_config
why: lib/core/database/tables/stage_definitions.dart and goals.dart both declare `trackId => integer().references(CurriculumTracks, #id)()` — a real, enforced FK. If a stage_definition/settings/goal Firestore snapshot merges before its curriculum_tracks row exists locally (independent per-collection listeners, or first-launch pull on a restored device), the raw insert throws an uncaught SqliteException(787) and aborts merging the whole page. BookmarkMerger (drift_merge_store.dart:527 `if (track == null) { ...skip... }`), GamificationSettingsMerger (gamification_settings_merger.dart:128 `if (localTrack == null) continue;`) and StudyDayConfigMerger (study_day_config_merger.dart:66 `if (trackExists == null) continue;`) already guard this exact race by skipping and relying on the next (idempotent) pull to re-merge — the pattern was never generalized to stage_definition/settings/goal, which resolve the identical remote-track-id-fallback (`localTrack?.id ?? remoteTrackId`) without ever checking the fallback actually exists.
recommendation: Add the same trackExists-before-insert guard (skip, don't throw; rely on idempotent re-merge next pull) to DriftMergeStore._upsertStageDefinition, _upsertSettings, and GoalMerger.merge, mirroring StudyDayConfigMerger's existing pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: merge a stage_definition (and separately a settings, and a goal) row referencing a curriculum_id with no local curriculum_tracks row yet — assert no exception is thrown and the row is silently skipped.
Same test seeds the track afterward and re-merges the identical row — assert it now applies (idempotent recovery).
New regression tests live under test/core/sync/merge/, mirroring the FK-race coverage style already present for bookmark/study_day_config.

corrections: The finding understates that this is already partially bounded: sync_orchestrator.dart wraps every pull step (`step()` at ~L759, `log()` in `_buildRecoveryPullTriggers` at ~L1449) and the real-time listener dispatch (`_onListenerEvent` at ~L1373 `.catchError(...)`) in outer catch-alls that log-and-swallow local DB errors, so this does NOT crash the app or abort other collections' sync — it's non-fatal and self-heals (tracks are pulled before stage_definitions/goals in the launch-pull step order, so a full relaunch/resume pull resolves it). The real, still-valid defect is coarser-grained: one bad row in a listener snapshot or pull page currently drops the *entire* batch of legitimate stage_definition/goal/settings rows for that dispatch, not just the offending row — exactly the failure mode the sibling per-row guards were added to prevent. Recommendation and acceptance criteria remain correct as written.

The finding's phrase 'uncaught SqliteException(787)' is uncaught only at the merger/router level - sync_orchestrator.dart:~780 has a defense-in-depth catch (_isLocalDatabaseError) that swallows it per-step, logs 'sync_pull_step_db_error_nonfatal', and lets the sync session continue, so this does not crash the app or abort the whole session, only that one step's page for that cycle (self-heals next pull). Severity/verdict unaffected.
